title: Cap. V Obj. 8: none can be saved without faith — therefore election from foresight faith
latin: Obj. 8. Qui secundum Dei voluntatem absque fide salvari non potest, non praedestinatur salvandus sine fide. Nulla est enim arcana Dei voluntas quae adversatur revelatae. Revelata dicit, Nolo Petrum salvare absque fide: Non est ergo arcana voluntas quae decernit eundem Petrum servare absque fide: ac proinde electio ad salutem est ex fide praevisa.
pass_a: Objection 8. He who according to the will of God cannot be saved without faith is not predestinated to be saved without faith. For there is no secret will of God which is adverse to the revealed. The revealed says, I will not save Peter without faith: There is therefore no secret will which decrees to save the same Peter without faith: and accordingly election unto salvation is from foresight faith.
pass_b: Obj. 8. Whoever by God's will cannot be saved without faith is not predestinated to be saved without faith. There is no secret will of God adverse to the revealed. The revealed says, I will not save Peter without faith — so there is no secret will decreeing to save that same Peter without faith. Therefore election unto salvation is from foresight faith.

lemmas.gloss: I will not save Peter without faith

title: Cap. V Obj. 8 Sol: adults not saved or predestinated without faith — but distinguish praedestinare/servare
latin: Sol. Agnoscimus, adultorum neminem absque fide salvari posse, idque quia Divina voluntas ita ordinavit; quam voluntatis suae ordinationem in Evangelio patefecit et promulgavit. Concedimus etiam, neminem adultorum praedestinari salvandum sine fide. Sed hoc ambigue sumi potest; eget itaque distincta explicatione. Cum igitur praedestinare denotat actum internum in arcano mentis Divinae, Servare effectum externum in homine operatum: dicimus, neminem praedestinari salvandum absque fidei antecedentis consideratione, sub ratione medii ad productionem effectus illius externi: sed negamus, neminem praedestinari salvandum absque consideratione fidei antecedentis sub ratione motivi, ad productionem actus illius interni.
pass_a: Solution. We acknowledge that no adult can be saved without faith, and that because the Divine will has so ordained; which ordination of his will he has opened and promulgated in the Gospel. We also concede that no adult is predestinated to be saved without faith. But this can be taken ambiguously; it therefore needs a distinct explanation. Since therefore to predestinate denotes an internal act in the secret of the Divine mind, to Save an external effect wrought in the man: we say that no one is predestinated to be saved without consideration of antecedent faith, under the reason of a means unto the production of that external effect: but we deny that no one is predestinated to be saved without consideration of antecedent faith under the reason of a motive, unto the production of that internal act.
pass_b: Sol. We grant no adult can be saved without faith — so God's will ordained, and he opened that ordination in the Gospel. We also grant no adult is predestinated to be saved without faith. But that can be taken ambiguously and needs distinct explanation. Predestinating denotes an internal act in the secret of the divine mind; Saving denotes an external effect wrought in the man. So: no one is predestinated to be saved without considering antecedent faith as a means to producing that external effect — but we deny that no one is predestinated to be saved without considering antecedent faith as a motive for producing that internal act.

lemmas.gloss: faith as means vs as motive

title: Cap. V Obj. 8 Sol: God saves through faith — cause of the willed, not of the willing
latin: Deus salvat per fidem, et Deus decernit servare per fidem; ita tamen ut fides intelligatur habere respectum causae vel conditionis antecedentis, non quoad ipsum decretum, sed quoad rem decretam. Effectus Divinae voluntatis potest procedere ex aliqua causa quam Deus ab aeterno praescivit, ipsumque ordinem causae ad causatum voluit: Et hoc dicitur causa voliti, non volendi.
pass_a: God saves through faith, and God decrees to save through faith; yet so that faith is understood to have the respect of an antecedent cause or condition, not as to the decree itself, but as to the thing decreed. The effect of the Divine will can proceed from some cause which God foresaw from eternity, and willed the very order of the cause unto the caused: And this is called a cause of the thing willed, not of the willing.
pass_b: God saves through faith, and decrees to save through faith — yet so that faith counts as an antecedent cause or condition not of the decree itself, but of the thing decreed. An effect of the divine will can proceed from a cause God foresaw from eternity and whose order to the caused he willed: that is called a cause of the thing willed, not of the willing.

lemmas.gloss: cause of the willed, not of willing

title: Cap. V Obj. 8 Sol: revealed will does not make faith a motive of the eternal good pleasure
latin: Neque hac distinctione nostra collidimus arcanam voluntatem revelatae: Revelata siquidem dicit, Nolo Petrum salvare absque fide (scilicet praecedente, ut medio ad salutem ejus efficiendam ordinato): at revelata non dicit, Nolo Petrum servare absque fide praecedente tanquam motivo vel conditione ad formandum meum de ejusdem salute aeternum beneplacitum. Non igitur ex revelata Dei voluntate recte deducitur electio Petri ad salutem facta ex fide ejusdem antecedanea.
pass_a: Nor by this distinction of ours do we make the secret will collide with the revealed: For the revealed indeed says, I will not save Peter without faith (namely preceding, as a means ordained unto effecting his salvation): but the revealed does not say, I will not save Peter without faith preceding as a motive or condition for forming my eternal good pleasure concerning the salvation of the same. It is not therefore rightly deduced from the revealed will of God that the election of Peter unto salvation was made from his antecedent faith.
pass_b: Nor does our distinction set the secret will against the revealed. The revealed does say, I will not save Peter without faith — namely preceding faith as a means ordained to effect his salvation. It does not say, I will not save Peter without preceding faith as a motive or condition for forming my eternal good pleasure about his salvation. So from the revealed will one cannot rightly deduce that Peter's election unto salvation was made from his antecedent faith.

lemmas.gloss: faith as means not as motive of decree

title: Cap. V Obj. 8 Sol close: faith and perseverance flow from election — Cap. V Arminian objections end
latin: Imo ex revelato Dei verbo recte deducitur, tum fidem, tum in fide perseverantiam ex praeeunte electione sive ad vitam ordinatione dependere. Huc spectant illa, Actor. xiii. 48. Crediderunt, quotquot ordinati erant ad vitam aeternam. Matth. xxiv. 24. Seductores in apostasiam pertraherent, si possibile esset, ipsos electos. Quod igitur quidam credunt, et quod credentes a fide non resiliunt, id ex antecedente electione dimanat: non, ut vult Arminius, quod quidem praevidentur credituri et in fide perseveraturi, exinde eorundem prae aliis electio dimanat. Plures ex Arminii scriptis objectiones non congeremus, quia hisce dissipatis, facile est et reliquas omnes, quae ejusdem farinae sunt, dissolvere. Veniemus igitur tandem ad defensionem nostram exponendam, et argumentis roborandam.
pass_a: Nay from the revealed word of God it is rightly deduced that both faith and perseverance in faith depend upon a preceding election or ordination unto life. Hither look those places, Acts 13:48. As many as were ordained to eternal life believed. Matt. 24:24. Seducers would draw even the elect into apostasy, if it were possible. That therefore certain ones believe, and that believers do not spring back from faith, that flows from antecedent election: not, as Arminius wills, that because they are indeed foreseen as about to believe and about to persevere in faith, from thence their election before others flows. We will not heap up more objections from the writings of Arminius, because these being scattered, it is easy also to dissolve all the rest, which are of the same flour. We will therefore at length come to setting forth our defense, and strengthening it with arguments.
pass_b: Indeed from God's revealed word it is rightly deduced that both faith and perseverance in faith depend on a preceding election or ordination unto life. So Acts 13:48 — as many as were ordained to eternal life believed — and Matt. 24:24 — seducers would draw even the elect into apostasy if it were possible. That some believe, and that believers do not spring back from faith, flows from antecedent election — not, as Arminius wills, that foresight of their believing and persevering is what makes their election flow before others. We will not heap more objections from Arminius's writings; these scattered, the rest of the same flour are easy to dissolve. We come at last to set out our defense and strengthen it with arguments.
